Iran’s IRGC issued a statement accusing the United States and Israel of violating international law by attacking Iran and killing Ali Khamenei and senior commanders. 

The statement described the deaths as martyrdom and said the strikes would not weaken Iran or the so-called “Resistance Front,” but instead strengthen it.

On behalf of resistance forces, the Quds Force pledged to continue fighting what it called “global arrogance and international Zionism,” framing the response as a religious duty.

 It warned that Israel and the United States would face retaliation and would find no safety anywhere in the world, vowing to continue resistance and avenge those killed.

The IDF announced it carried out a wave of strikes in Lebanon targeting assets belonging to the al-Qard al-Hasan Association, which it describes as a key financial arm of Hezbollah. 

According to the IDF, the association operates under the guise of a civilian financial institution but in practice supports Hezbollah by managing deposits, paying salaries to operatives, and facilitating transfers of Iranian funds.

The military said Hezbollah uses this parallel financial network to fund weapons purchases, production, and operational activities, while exploiting Lebanon’s ongoing economic crisis to deepen public dependency and sustain its military infrastructure.
